forms: pick a cause of fire
say which is a natural and which a human cause
say what a fire needs
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.FOUNDA.FIRE_SAFETY.FIRE_CAUSES.mastery: The child names causes of fire (a lit candle or match left unattended, faulty or overloaded electrical wiring, an unattended cooking fire or stove, careless disposal of cigarettes, leaking gas, children playing with matches, lightning and dry grass in the hot sun) and does not say fires have only natural causes. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the way to prevent a fire
say what to do with matches and fuel
say what to do with wiring and exits
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.FOUNDA.FIRE_SAFETY.FIRE_PREVENT.mastery: The child picks ways to prevent fire (keep matches and lighters away from children, store paraffin, petrol and gas safely away from heat, never leave a stove or candle unattended, repair damaged wires, do not overload sockets, keep exits clear and have a fire drill) and does not block exits or store fuel near a stove. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say why data is valuable
pick a threat to data
say what a virus does
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.FOUNDA.DATA_SAFETY.DATA_THREATS.mastery: The child says data (documents, photos, messages, schoolwork) is valuable because it is hard to replace and may be private, and names threats (viruses and other malware, theft or loss of the device, hackers, power failure, accidental deletion, a spoilt storage device), and does not say a virus can only come from the internet. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the way to protect data
say what a good password is
say what a backup is
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.FOUNDA.DATA_SAFETY.DATA_PROTECT.mastery: The child picks ways to protect data (a strong password that is kept secret, a backup copy on another device, antivirus software kept up to date, locking the screen, not opening unknown links or attachments, keeping the device safe) and does not share a password or keep only one copy. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the instrument for a task
say what the set square does
say what the compass does
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_INSTR.mastery: The child names the T-square (draws horizontal lines), set squares of 45 and 30/60 degrees (draw upright and slanted lines), the compass (draws circles and arcs), the protractor (measures angles), the ruler (measures lengths), the drawing board, a hard pencil for fine lines and the eraser, and does not mix them up. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the part of the sheet
say where the title block goes
say the size of an A4 sheet
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.mastery: The child says a drawing sheet has a border (a frame drawn a little inside the edges), a title block (name, title, scale, date and sheet number) at the bottom right, a clear working area, and that A4 is 297 by 210 millimetres, and does not put the title block at the top or leave out the border. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the line from its job
say where the figure is placed
pick the unit used
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.mastery: The child names the dimension line (a thin line with arrowheads showing the size), extension lines (thin lines that stretch out from the object), the leader line (points to a note), the figure (written above the dimension line), the symbols for diameter and radius, and says sizes on drawings are normally in millimetres, and does not use the object line as a dimension line. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: read the overall length
work out a missing dimension
work out the diameter from the radius
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.mastery: The child reads a dimension from the drawing, adds the parts to get the overall length, subtracts to find a missing part, says the diameter is twice the radius, and keeps the unit with the answer. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what a scale means
work out the real length
work out the drawing length
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.mastery: The child says a scale such as 1:50 means one unit on the drawing stands for 50 of the same unit on the real object, multiplies a drawing length by the scale to get the real length and divides a real length by the scale to get the drawing length, knows 1:1 is full size and 2:1 is an enlargement, and keeps the units. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a visual programming tool
pick a feature of such a tool
say what a loop or an event does
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.COMMUN.VISUAL_PROGRAMMING.VISUAL.mastery: The child says visual programming builds programs by snapping together blocks instead of typing code, names tools such as Scratch and App Inventor, names features (a block palette, a script area, a stage with sprites, events, loops and decisions), and says a loop repeats instructions. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the composite material
pick what it is made of
pick its use
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.MATERI.COMPOSITE_MATERIALS.COMPO.mastery: The child says a composite material joins two or more materials to get a better one, and names concrete (cement, sand, ballast and water), reinforced concrete (concrete with steel bars), plywood (thin layers of wood glued crosswise), fibreglass (glass fibre in resin), and mud and straw bricks, with uses (buildings and slabs, furniture and boards, boat hulls and tanks, walls), and does not call concrete a single material. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the ceramic material
pick its property
pick its use
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.MATERI.CERAMIC_MATERIALS.CERAMIC.mastery: The child names ceramics (clay pots, bricks, floor and wall tiles, porcelain cups and sinks, electrical insulators), says they are hard, brittle (they break or crack when hit or dropped), resist heat and corrosion and do not conduct electricity, and says tiles, bricks, sinks and insulators use these properties. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the tool for a task
pick the way to care for the tool
say what a blunt tool does
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.CUTTING_TOOLS.CUT_TOOLS.mastery: The child picks the hacksaw for metal, the tenon saw for wood, the coping saw for curves, the chisel for shaping wood, the plane for smoothing wood, the tin snips for sheet metal and scissors for card and cloth, and picks care (keep blades sharp and clean, oil steel blades, store with guards, carry points down) and does not use a wood saw on metal. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: sort the software
pick the application for a task
say what an operating system does
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.mastery: The child says system software runs the computer (an operating system such as Windows, Android or Linux), application software does a task for the user (a word processor for letters, a spreadsheet for calculations, a presentation program for slides, a browser for the web, a database for records), utility software looks after the computer (antivirus), and that software cannot be touched while hardware can. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say why records matter
sort a transaction
sort cash and credit
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.mastery: The child says a business keeps records to know its income, spending, profit or loss, to plan, to pay tax and to get loans, and sorts transactions into cash (paid now) and credit (paid later), income and expenditure, and assets (what a business owns), liabilities (what it owes) and capital (what the owner put in). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a source of income
say why a budget matters
pick an ethical or unethical practice
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.mastery: The child names sources of income (wages or a salary, profit from a business, sales of farm produce, gifts and pocket money, interest), says a budget plans the income and spending so that needs come first and some is saved, and tells an honest budget from an unethical practice (hiding spending, using money meant for something else, borrowing without a plan to repay, cheating others). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say why marketing matters
pick a source of market information
pick a factor in choosing a market
pick a tool of marketing
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.mastery: The child says marketing helps a business find customers and sell, names sources of market information (asking customers, watching competitors, a survey, the internet, newspapers and radio), names factors in choosing a market (customer demand, price, location, competition, transport) and tools (a poster, radio, social media, samples, a price offer, word of mouth). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the intermediary
put the channel in order
pick the ethical practice
find the false step in a learner's reason
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..mastery: The child names intermediaries (wholesalers who sell in bulk to retailers, retailers who sell to buyers, agents who bring buyers and sellers together), puts channels in order (producer to consumer; producer to retailer to consumer; producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer), and picks ethical practices (honest weights and measures, fair prices, safe delivery, not hoarding) over unethical ones. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
